essence: Distinct from every lit thing, light itself does not shine as an object — too pervasive to appear; illumined-vs-illuminator is mere convention.

sections.SUMMARY: Distinct from every lit thing, light itself does not shine as an object — too pervasive to appear; illumined-vs-illuminator is mere convention.
sections.FUNCTION: Establishes light as unobjectifiable; subject-object vocabulary demoted.
sections.KEY TERMS:
* **arkendudīpādi** — sun-moon-lamp-and-the-rest
* **avabhāsa** — illumination
* **ativyāptatā** — over-pervasion
* **prakāśarūpa** — of the nature of light
* **prakāśyaprakāśatā** — illumined-illuminator
* **vyavahāra** — convention
sections.EXPLANATION: Distinct (bhinnam) from the illumination (avabhāsa) of sun, moon, lamp and the rest (arkendudīpādi), it does not shine (na ābhāti) — on account of over-pervasion (ativyāptatayā): too pervasive to show up as an object, like sight itself never seen. And hence (tataḥ): it is of the nature of light, just this much (iyat) — illumined and illuminator named is convention (vyavahāra) merely (eva). The subject-object vocabulary is demoted; what is, is light, unobjectifiable because everywhere.
sections.BOUNDARY: Whether 'iyat' (just this much) limits or affirms is unresolved.
sections.RELATED: * Paramārthacarcā v.2 — nothing apart from knowledge.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is knowledge (jñāna) in the mode of demotion of subject-object; the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at light's over-pervasion.
